items.text: Under the Michigan energy code, what is the maximum U-factor for a skylight in any Michigan climate zone?
B. 0.55 — Table N1102.1.1 sets the skylight U-factor maximum at 0.55 in all Michigan zones; 0.32 is the window/door value.
What is the maximum U-factor for windows and doors (fenestration) in all Michigan climate zones?
C. 0.32 — Table N1102.1.1 caps fenestration U-factor at 0.32 in zones 5A, 6A, and 7; 0.30 is the 2021 IECC trap, which is not in force.
A new house is built in climate zone 6A (northern Lower Peninsula). What ceiling insulation is required?
D. R-49 — Table N1102.1.1 requires R-49 ceilings in zones 6A and 7; R-38 is the Michigan-amended value for zone 5A only.
In climate zone 7 (western Upper Peninsula), what R-value is required for a floor over an unconditioned space?
A. R-38 — Table N1102.1.1 requires R-38 floors in zone 7; R-30 is the zone 5A and 6A floor value.
What basement wall insulation satisfies the energy code in climate zone 5A?
B. R-10 continuous or R-13 cavity — Table N1102.1.1 requires 10/13 (R-10 continuous or R-13 cavity) basement walls in zone 5A; 15/19 is the zones 6A-7 and crawl space value, a listed trap.
What slab edge insulation does the energy code require in climate zone 5A?
A. R-10 to a depth of 2 feet — Table N1102.1.1 requires R-10 slab edge insulation 2 feet deep in zone 5A; the 4-foot depth applies in zones 6A and 7.
In the energy table's basement wall notation '10/13', what do the two numbers mean?

C. Continuous insulation first, cavity insulation second - either one satisfies — Per Table N1102.1.1, the first number is continuous insulation and the second is cavity insulation, and either alone satisfies the requirement.
What SHGC (solar heat gain coefficient) limit applies to windows in Michigan?

D. None - SHGC is marked NR (not required) in zones 5 through 8 — Table N1102.1.1 marks SHGC as NR in zones 5-8 because it is a southern-climate requirement; any numeric SHGC is a Michigan trap answer.
Which insulation material has the HIGHEST approximate R-value per inch?
B. Closed-cell spray foam — Industry-standard values: closed-cell spray foam runs about R-6 to R-6.5 per inch, versus fiberglass about 3.2, cellulose about 3.5, and open-cell about 3.6.
Baffles at eave vents must maintain what minimum airspace between the insulation and the roof sheathing?
A. 1 inch — R806.3 requires a minimum 1-inch airspace between the insulation and the roof sheathing at the vents.
Kraft-faced fiberglass batts serve as what class of vapor retarder?
C. Class II — Under R702.7, Class II covers 0.1 to 1.0 perm materials such as kraft-faced batts; polyethylene and foil facings are Class I, and paint is Class III.
In climate zone 5, a builder wants to use only latex paint (Class III) as the vapor retarder on a 2x6 wall without vented cladding. What continuous insulated sheathing makes this legal?
D. R-7.5 — Table R702.7.1 permits Class III in zone 5 with R-7.5 continuous insulated sheathing over a 2x6 wall (R-5 is the 2x4 value); R-11.25 is the zone 6 2x6 value.
A framer suggests wrapping the OUTSIDE of the frame walls in polyethylene sheeting before siding 'for extra protection.' What is wrong with this?

A. Class I poly on the exterior side is prohibited practice - it creates a double vapor barrier that traps moisture — Per R702.7, the Class I or II retarder belongs on the interior warm-in-winter side; Class I poly on the exterior creates a double vapor barrier and trapped-moisture condition.
What is the base net free ventilating area required for a vented attic?
B. 1 to 150 of the attic floor area — R806.2 sets the base attic ventilation ratio at 1/150 of the attic floor area, reducible to 1/300 when a qualifying condition is met.
A builder in climate zone 5A wants to use the reduced 1-to-300 attic vent ratio. How can he qualify?

C. Locate 40 to 50 percent of the vent area in the upper portion, within 3 feet of the ridge, with the balance at the eaves — R806.2 allows 1/300 with either condition alone, but the ceiling vapor-retarder path applies only in zones 6, 7, and 8, so zone 5A must use the 40-50 percent upper-vent placement.
A 2,200 sq ft house with 3 bedrooms needs whole-house mechanical ventilation. What continuous rate does the code table require?
D. 60 cfm — Table M1507.3.3(1) requires 60 cfm continuous for 1,501-3,000 sq ft with 2-3 bedrooms.
Where must a bathroom exhaust fan discharge?

A. Directly to the outdoors - never into an attic, soffit, ridge vent, or crawl space — M1501.1 requires all exhaust to discharge to the outdoors, never into an attic, soffit, ridge vent, or crawl space.
What local exhaust rates does the code require for a KITCHEN?
B. 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous — Table M1507.4 requires 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous for kitchens; 50/20 are the bathroom numbers and the trap.
What is the EPA action level for radon in a home?
C. 4.0 picocuries per liter — The EPA action level is 4.0 pCi/L - an EPA guidance number, not an MRC number.
What is the maximum sill height above the floor for an emergency escape and rescue opening?
D. 44 inches — R310.1 caps the sill of an emergency escape and rescue opening at 44 inches above the floor.
When must a window well serving an egress window have a permanently affixed ladder or steps?

A. When the well is deeper than 44 inches — R310.2 requires a permanently affixed ladder or steps when the window well is deeper than 44 inches; the well itself must be at least 9 sq ft with a 36-inch projection and width.
How must an emergency escape and rescue opening operate?

B. From the inside without keys, tools, or special knowledge — R310 requires the opening to be operational from the inside without keys, tools, or special knowledge; bars or grilles are allowed only if releasable the same way.
A fixed 12 sq ft window has its bottom edge 12 inches above the floor, top edge 60 inches above the floor, and a hallway runs directly alongside it. No door is nearby. Is safety glazing required?

C. Yes - it exceeds 9 sq ft, bottom edge under 18 inches, top edge over 36 inches, and a walking surface is within 36 inches, meeting all four conditions — R308.4.3 requires safety glazing when all four conditions are met: over 9 sq ft, bottom edge under 18 inches, top edge over 36 inches, and a walking surface within 36 inches horizontally.
When does glazing installed in a guard or railing require safety glazing?

A. Always - glazing in guards and railings is a hazardous location in every case — R308.4 lists glazing in guards and railings as a hazardous location requiring safety glazing in every case, with no size or location threshold.
A window over a bathtub has its bottom edge 50 inches above the tub drain. Does it need safety glazing?

D. Yes - wet-location glazing with a bottom edge less than 60 inches above the drain must be safety glazed — R308.4.5 requires safety glazing in wet locations where the bottom edge is less than 60 inches above the drain or standing surface and within 60 inches horizontally of the water's edge.
What minimum clear size must the required egress door of a dwelling provide?
A. 32 inches wide by 78 inches high — R311.2 requires at least one side-hinged exterior door with 32 inches clear width and 78 inches clear height.
A plan shows the house-to-garage door opening directly into a bedroom. The door is 20-minute fire-rated and self-closing. What is the problem?

B. The door may NEVER open into a sleeping room, regardless of rating — R302.5.1 prohibits the garage-to-dwelling door from opening into a sleeping room, even when it is a compliant 1-3/8-inch solid or 20-minute self-closing door.
A garage has a bedroom directly above it. What must the garage ceiling receive?

C. Five-eighths inch Type X gypsum on the garage side — Table R302.6 requires 5/8-inch Type X on a garage ceiling with habitable space above, and the structure supporting that floor gets 1/2-inch gypsum; this is a separation, not a rated assembly.
Without adhesive, what is the maximum nail spacing for gypsum board on a CEILING?
D. 7 inches — Table R702.3.5 requires ceiling nails at 7 inches (screws 12 inches); 8 and 16 inches are the wall spacings and the trap.
A hallway will get semi-gloss paint under strong window light. What drywall finish level should be specified?

A. Level 5 - three coats plus a skim coat over the entire surface — Under the GA-214 finish levels, Level 5 (three coats plus a full skim coat) is specified for gloss or semi-gloss paint and critical lighting; Level 4 is standard paint.
